messages.subject: Rhat for stanfit objects
parts:
Hi,

How can I query the Rhat for a stanfit object in rstan? The print method
displays it, but I would like to access it for a plot. I looked at the
code but got lost, it seems to be saving it somewhere in a cache.

By the way, maybe it could print more digits by default? Rhat=1 is
reassuring, but I am always wondering whether that is 1.4 or 1.004,
rounded to 1. I found that

print(fit, digits=4)

prints the whole thing, but maybe two digits after the decimal dot by
default would be informative.

Best,

Tamas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Rhat for stanfit objects
parts:
On 2/5/14, 2:04 PM, Tamas Papp wrote:
> Hi,
>
> How can I query the Rhat for a stanfit object in rstan? The print method
> displays it, but I would like to access it for a plot. I looked at the
> code but got lost, it seems to be saving it somewhere in a cache.

If fit is the stanfit object, you can use summary(fit)$summary
to pull out the summary statistics.

For example,

> labels(summary(fit)$summary)
[[1]]
[1] "y" "lp__"

[[2]]
[1] "mean" "se_mean" "sd" "2.5%" "25%" "50%" "75%" "97.5%" "n_eff" "Rhat"

First arg is variable and second arg is summary stats.

And then

> summary(fit)$summary[1,10]
[1] 1.001408

gives you the Rhat for y. I'm sure there's a more elegant way to do this
in R.

> By the way, maybe it could print more digits by default? Rhat=1 is
> reassuring, but I am always wondering whether that is 1.4 or 1.004,
> rounded to 1. I found that
>
> print(fit, digits=4)
>
> prints the whole thing, but maybe two digits after the decimal dot by
> default would be informative.
>

Thanks for the reminder. We've been meaning to do that. I created
an issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/issues/44

We want to go with digits=3 in order to test Rhat < 1.05, which is
Andrew's default recommendation. He likes fewer digits, but we've
compromised on 3.

- Bob
